note: BUMPED to 1.0.12 from 1.0.11. THE TRANSCRIPTION, THE SECTION MODEL AND THE ANCHORS ARE UNCHANGED: source.txt is byte-identical to 1.0.11's (sha256 748e58cef10981193585a101fcf67951cc3a37577eaf756f08399e343e1dd8bf), and divisions.json and base.json are carried unchanged. THE RULES MOVE BY ONE MARK AND ONE CITATION. (1) r11904 IS WITHDRAWN AND RE-ISSUED as r11912: it served "οἱ παρὰ κλεινούς" with an ACUTE on the ultima, and that mark has NO INSTRUMENT anywhere in the record — the rule named no witness for it, and the unit that wrote it recorded that its own plate draw was truncated before the word. Read blind at the scanned item's OWN MAXIMUM RESOLUTION (the item serves each leaf at four times the stored scan: archive.org page/n11_w3000.jpg, 5367x7017, against the stored leaf's 1342x1755), the plate gives the GRAVE — google/gemini-2.5-flash in 3 of 4 independent draws (the fourth read no marks), Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B in 2 of 2, and the 955 review's two draws of the stored leaf on both — and NOT ONE DRAW OF ANY INSTRUMENT RETURNED THE ACUTE. The print's own convention graves a final acute before a following word, and the received text of Synesius Hymn 3 prints the grave. ONE REPORTING CORRECTION, SUPERSEDING AN EARLIER WORDING: the human-proofread Project Gutenberg witness is named in r11912's RATIONALE, not in its `witness` field — a rule's `witness` field names the plate — and an earlier report of this unit's undertaking said `witness`; that wording is superseded (the rule's own rationale states the standing of both names). (2) r11831's EVIDENCE LEAF IS RE-CITED n32 -> n31 — the one rule the 1.0.11 leaf pass could not place, now placed by SUBSTRING on the exact text-layer instrument (its find is WIDENED with its own leading space, " geous ", which is why a line-starting locator could not place it; " geous " occurs on exactly one line of the transcription, source line 1520, which is non-empty line 1054, which stands on archive leaf n31). Its reading does not change. (3) THE FOUR VERSE LINES OF PRINTED PAGE xvii ARE STILL NOT SERVED, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. 1.0.11 re-homed the six rules that had been serving another printed line's Greek, and the readings they had been serving over page xvii's OWN lines (the transcription's non-empty lines 323, 324, 326 and 328 — source lines 500, 501, 503 and 505) were then in no rule at all, so the page still reads half-restored. Their readings were re-measured on the plate for this version — 324 "τό, τε κυδῆεν" (the withdrawn rule's acute on the penult corrected to the circumflex every reader gives), 326 "ἔργα τὰ θνητῶν", 328 "διανισσόμενον," (all three agreed by every reader), and 323 "προχέει σειρά", where the plate readers DISAGREE on both words and the letters rest on the human-proofread transcription of the same print, confirmed on the plate by the first word's own component count and by the print's English of that Greek set below it — BUT A RULE SERVING THEM WOULD STAND UNBACKED IN THE PRESERVED FRONT-MATTER REGION. That region admits only rules the CLASSED Greek pass read (tools/echo-probe.mjs), and MEASURED: the pass's own draw cache holds NO USABLE draw at any of the FOUR lines that carry them — at 500, 501 and 505 no draw is keyed at the line at all, and the draw keyed at 503 read the line BELOW, so it carries line 504's text (its n12 keys list only 478, 479, 481, 502, 503, 504, 506, 507) — because it read the line BELOW each line it was asked about. The readings are recorded for the unit that extends the pass; none is invented here to make the page look complete. NOT ONE DIVISION OR ANCHOR MOVES: the pinned anchor manifest at this version is byte-identical to 1.0.11's. MEASURED by folding every rule of each version over its own transcription, in rule order, every occurrence: the two reading views differ in EXACTLY ONE LINE — the corrected mark — and nothing else.
